Disposal Method: Compost bin or community composting
Reason: Food scraps can decompose into nutrient-rich compost
Safety Guidance: Keep meat or dairy separate if local rules require it; never place food waste in plastic bags
Sustainability Impact: Composting returns nutrients to soil and reduces landfill methane

Disposal Method: Compost bin or home compost
Reason: Banana peels are biodegradable organic matter
Safety Guidance: Remove stickers and compost the peel; do not litter even though it is biodegradable
Sustainability Impact: Composting avoids landfill disposal and creates soil amendment

Disposal Method: Compost bin or community compost
Reason: Vegetable scraps break down naturally in a composting system
Safety Guidance: Drain excess liquid and remove produce stickers
Sustainability Impact: Composting reduces landfill volume and supports soil health

Disposal Method: Compost bin
Reason: Fruit scraps are biodegradable and suitable for most compost systems
Safety Guidance: Remove non-compostable packaging and check local accepted materials
Sustainability Impact: Composting helps close the organic nutrient cycle

Disposal Method: Compost bin or garden compost
Reason: Coffee grounds are organic and add carbon and nitrogen to compost
Safety Guidance: Let grounds cool and mix with other compost materials
Sustainability Impact: Composting diverts organic waste and can improve soil structure

Disposal Method: Compost bin
Reason: Tea leaves can decompose with other plant-based material
Safety Guidance: Remove staples and plastic tea bags before composting
Sustainability Impact: Composting keeps useful organic matter out of landfill

Disposal Method: Paper recycling bin
Reason: Clean paper fibers can be recovered into new paper products
Safety Guidance: Keep paper dry and remove plastic film or food residue
Sustainability Impact: Recycling saves trees water and energy compared with new paper

Disposal Method: Paper recycling bin
Reason: Newspaper is made from recyclable paper fibers
Safety Guidance: Keep it clean and dry; do not burn it
Sustainability Impact: Recycling extends fiber life and reduces demand for virgin pulp

Disposal Method: Flattened cardboard recycling bin
Reason: Cardboard fibers are widely recyclable when clean and dry
Safety Guidance: Flatten boxes and remove tape or food contamination where possible
Sustainability Impact: Recycling cardboard reduces landfill volume and raw material use

Disposal Method: Recycle clean sections and compost food-soiled sections
Reason: Cardboard can be recycled but grease and food residue affect paper quality
Safety Guidance: Separate heavily greasy parts and follow local guidance
Sustainability Impact: Sorting prevents contamination in paper recycling streams

Disposal Method: Check local cup recycling or general waste guidance
Reason: Many paper cups have a plastic lining that standard paper recycling cannot process
Safety Guidance: Empty the cup and do not place it in paper recycling unless accepted locally
Sustainability Impact: Specialized recovery can reduce composite packaging waste

Disposal Method: Compost if accepted or use general waste
Reason: Used paper towels are often too contaminated for paper recycling
Safety Guidance: Do not compost towels with chemicals or cleaning products
Sustainability Impact: Composting suitable towels reduces landfill waste

Disposal Method: Empty and rinse into a plastic recycling bin
Reason: Many beverage bottles are recyclable when separated from contents
Safety Guidance: Empty and flatten when local guidance allows; keep caps according to local rules
Sustainability Impact: Recycling recovers plastic and reduces demand for new material

Disposal Method: Rinse and place in accepted plastic recycling
Reason: Some rigid containers can be remade into new plastic products
Safety Guidance: Remove food residue and check the resin or local acceptance rules
Sustainability Impact: Recycling reduces plastic pollution and virgin plastic production

Disposal Method: Return to a soft-plastic collection point or use general waste
Reason: Thin film can jam sorting machinery and is not accepted in many curbside programs
Safety Guidance: Keep bags out of household recycling unless a dedicated program accepts them
Sustainability Impact: Soft-plastic recovery reduces litter and material loss

Disposal Method: Use a soft-plastic take-back point where available
Reason: Multi-layer wrappers are difficult to recycle in standard systems
Safety Guidance: Do not burn wrappers; check local collection options
Sustainability Impact: Specialized collection can prevent persistent plastic litter

Disposal Method: Empty and place in a glass recycling container
Reason: Glass can be recycled repeatedly without losing quality
Safety Guidance: Handle broken glass carefully and keep it out of mixed recycling if required
Sustainability Impact: Glass recycling saves raw materials and energy

Disposal Method: Empty rinse and place in glass recycling
Reason: Glass jars are commonly accepted in glass recovery programs
Safety Guidance: Remove food contents and lids according to local rules
Sustainability Impact: Recycling glass reduces extraction of sand and other raw materials

Category: General waste or special glass collection
Disposal Method: Wrap securely and follow local broken-glass guidance
Reason: Broken glass can injure workers and may not be accepted in bottle recycling
Safety Guidance: Wrap in thick paper or a rigid container and label it; never place loose shards in a bag
Sustainability Impact: Safe collection protects people and keeps recycling streams usable

Disposal Method: Empty and rinse into a metal or mixed recycling bin
Reason: Steel and aluminum can be recovered and remelted
Safety Guidance: Do not crush cans if local sorting requires their shape; keep them free of food
Sustainability Impact: Metal recycling saves significant energy compared with mining new ore

Disposal Method: Recycle clean and balled foil where accepted
Reason: Clean aluminum foil can be recovered but loose tiny pieces are hard to sort
Safety Guidance: Rinse off food and make a fist-sized ball; otherwise use general waste
Sustainability Impact: Aluminum recovery saves energy and reduces mining impacts

Disposal Method: Donate reuse or place in a textile collection point
Reason: Usable textiles can serve another person and fibers may be recovered
Safety Guidance: Keep donations clean and dry; do not donate moldy or contaminated fabric
Sustainability Impact: Reuse reduces water energy and emissions from new textile production

Disposal Method: Donate or use a shoe and textile collection point
Reason: Many shoes can be reused or separated for material recovery
Safety Guidance: Pair shoes and keep them dry; do not donate unsafe or heavily contaminated footwear
Sustainability Impact: Reuse extends product life and reduces landfill waste

Disposal Method: Take to an authorized battery collection point
Reason: Batteries can leak and contain reactive materials that require controlled handling
Safety Guidance: Do not burn crush or place loose batteries in regular bins; tape exposed terminals
Sustainability Impact: Proper recovery prevents fires and captures valuable metals

Disposal Method: Use an authorized battery or e-waste drop-off
Reason: Lithium batteries can ignite if damaged or short-circuited
Safety Guidance: Do not puncture or throw in household bins; isolate damaged batteries and seek local hazardous-waste advice
Sustainability Impact: Specialized recycling reduces fire risk and recovers critical minerals

Disposal Method: Erase data and take to an authorized e-waste or electronics collection point
Reason: Phones contain recoverable metals and components needing specialized processing
Safety Guidance: Back up and factory-reset personal data; do not dismantle or burn the phone
Sustainability Impact: Recycling electronics recovers materials and reduces mining and toxic waste

Disposal Method: Take to an authorized e-waste collection point
Reason: Electronic components require specialized handling and material recovery
Safety Guidance: Do not dismantle burn or place in regular waste; coil cables safely
Sustainability Impact: Proper e-waste collection supports responsible recovery and disposal

Disposal Method: Use an electronics take-back or e-waste facility
Reason: Chargers contain wiring plastics and circuit components
Safety Guidance: Keep damaged cords away from water and do not cut or burn them
Sustainability Impact: Recovery reduces electronic waste and can reclaim copper and other materials

Disposal Method: Take to an authorized e-waste collection point
Reason: Small electronics contain mixed materials that are difficult to sort in regular recycling
Safety Guidance: Do not place in household recycling or attempt to burn them
Sustainability Impact: Responsible collection prevents persistent e-waste and recovers components

Disposal Method: Use an authorized e-waste recycler or manufacturer take-back
Reason: Devices contain metals plastics and sometimes batteries that need specialized handling
Safety Guidance: Remove personal data and keep batteries intact; follow local drop-off instructions
Sustainability Impact: Recycling recovers materials and helps prevent hazardous pollution

Disposal Method: Donate if usable or take to an authorized e-waste recycler
Reason: Laptops contain valuable metals and data-bearing storage
Safety Guidance: Back up and securely erase data; do not dismantle a swollen battery
Sustainability Impact: Reuse and material recovery reduce the footprint of new electronics

Disposal Method: Return through a cartridge take-back program
Reason: Cartridges contain mixed plastics ink and residual chemicals
Safety Guidance: Seal leaking cartridges and never pour ink into drains
Sustainability Impact: Take-back programs recover parts and reduce plastic waste

Disposal Method: Return to a pharmacy or authorized medicine take-back program
Reason: Medicines can contaminate water and harm people or animals if misused
Safety Guidance: Do not flush or share medicines; keep them in original packaging and follow local instructions
Sustainability Impact: Safe take-back prevents pharmaceutical pollution and accidental exposure

Disposal Method: Use an approved sharps container or local medical-waste service
Reason: Needles can injure people and transmit infection
Safety Guidance: Do not recap bend or place loose syringes in any household bin
Sustainability Impact: Specialized treatment protects sanitation workers and the community

Disposal Method: Place in a closed general-waste bin
Reason: Used tissues may carry germs and are not suitable for paper recycling
Safety Guidance: Wash hands and never recycle tissues; compost only if local guidance explicitly allows it
Sustainability Impact: Correct disposal reduces contamination and hygiene risks

Disposal Method: Seal and place in general waste
Reason: Diapers contain mixed absorbent materials and biological contamination
Safety Guidance: Wrap securely and wash hands after handling
Sustainability Impact: Safe disposal supports public hygiene and avoids contaminating recycling

Disposal Method: Use general waste only after separating recoverable materials
Reason: Mixed materials are difficult to recover and can contaminate recycling
Safety Guidance: Do not mix batteries medicines chemicals or e-waste with general waste
Sustainability Impact: Better sorting reduces landfill use and improves recovery rates

Disposal Method: Check local foam collection or use general waste
Reason: Expanded foam is bulky and rarely accepted in standard recycling
Safety Guidance: Keep foam out of drains and do not burn it
Sustainability Impact: Specialized recovery reduces persistent plastic litter

Disposal Method: Take leftover paint to a household hazardous-waste program
Reason: Paint can contain solvents and should not enter drains or regular recycling
Safety Guidance: Keep sealed and never pour paint into soil or water; follow local rules
Sustainability Impact: Proper treatment prevents chemical pollution and may enable material recovery

Disposal Method: Use an authorized hazardous-waste collection channel
Reason: Chemicals can harm people waterways and waste workers
Safety Guidance: Keep in original labeled containers and never mix chemicals
Sustainability Impact: Safe treatment prevents toxic releases and protects water quality

Disposal Method: Collect in a sealed container for an oil collection point or approved reuse
Reason: Used oil can clog drains and harm waterways
Safety Guidance: Let it cool and never pour it down a sink
Sustainability Impact: Recovery can produce biodiesel and prevents sewer or water pollution

Disposal Method: Reuse donate or take untreated wood to a local recovery facility
Reason: Untreated wood can be reused or chipped while treated wood may contain chemicals
Safety Guidance: Do not burn painted or treated wood; keep nails contained
Sustainability Impact: Reuse and chipping reduce landfill volume and demand for new timber

Disposal Method: Take fluorescent or LED bulbs to a designated collection point
Reason: Bulbs can contain mercury or electronic components and break easily
Safety Guidance: Handle carefully and do not place fluorescent bulbs in regular glass recycling
Sustainability Impact: Specialty recovery keeps hazardous materials out of landfill

Disposal Method: Compost small amounts where accepted or use general waste
Reason: Hair is organic but may not be accepted by every compost program
Safety Guidance: Keep free of chemical treatments and confirm local compost rules
Sustainability Impact: Composting or reuse avoids unnecessary landfill disposal

Disposal Method: Wash and keep using or donate
Reason: Durable bottles are designed to replace single-use containers
Safety Guidance: Repair or recycle only when the bottle is no longer usable
Sustainability Impact: Reuse avoids repeated packaging production and disposal

Disposal Method: Empty rinse and sort according to material and local campus rules
Reason: Food residue contaminates otherwise recyclable containers
Safety Guidance: Use a refillable container when possible and separate leftovers
Sustainability Impact: Correct sorting improves campus recovery and reduces single-use waste
